title: Luonnontieteellisen museon Elämän historia -sali sulkeutuu vuodenvaihteen jälkeen – uusi näyttely avautuu loppuvuodesta 2028
content:
The Natural History Museum’s History of Life is one of the museum’s most popular exhibitions. However, the exhibition, completed in 2008, has long been in need of an update, as it is outdated both in terms of content and exhibition technology.

– The new exhibition will present evolution and the development of biodiversity in a more spectacular and tangible way than before. This is the museum’s most significant renewal project in years, says Sanna Vuori, Head of the Public Engagement Unit at the Finnish Museum of Natural History.

The dinosaurs Giganotosaurus carolinii and Shunosaurus lii in the History of Life exhibition have become familiar to many museum visitors over the years. They will remain in the new exhibition but will be joined by never-before-seen reconstructions of prehistoric animals. Among other things, a reconstruction of the otter-like early whale Ambulocetus natans is currently being built in the museum’s conservation facilities.

title: Southnord Artfest 2026: Roots En Route
content:
Roots En Route is a multi-sensory installation by four artists who will create a multi-sensory installation in dialogue with the greenhouses – examining rootedness and displacement; asking what grows where it was planted and what survives the crossing. The African plants that fill the greenhouses carry their own histories of movement and adaptation.

Camille Norment in collaboration with Sofia Jernberg create a soundscape drawing on the insects and birds of the plants' homelands. Toubab Holmes' site-specific scent installation traces the hidden journeys of plants through the extractive system of perfumery. Charmaine Watkiss visits the botanical legacies and healing traditions of her Caribbean ancestry through large-scale drawings of Plant Warriors. Together, the three works read the botanical garden as an archive of movement, and the plants in it as things that were carried, taken and made to travel.

Running from October 2026 through January 2027, the exhibition offers a long, unhurried encounter between art and the plant world. Set aside more time than you think you need. Walk slowly, sense carefully, and let yourself be immersed.

title: “Ilman pölyttäjiä maailma olisi ankea ja väritön” – Uusi näyttely avaa oven pölyttäjien kiehtovaan elämään
content:
Pollinators represent an astonishingly diverse group of animals, many of which possess remarkable abilities despite their small size. Bees can count, bumblebees solve problems, and on distant islands, even lizards can pollinate flowers.

The  exhibition, which combines science and art, offers a wealth of information, stunning visuals, and fun activities for visitors of all ages. Guests can play interactive games like "Identify the Pollinators" and "Pollinator Protection Bingo," design their own imaginary pollinator, and explore the museum's impressive collection of specimens. The exhibition is based on a newly illustrated non-fiction book.

– We want to show the world through the eyes of pollinators, says exhibition scriptwriter Mia Rönkä, Adjunct Professor in Environmental Ecology at the University of Turku. Rönkä has written the exhibition’s informational texts and poems.

Although the sensory perceptions, cognitive abilities, and communication methods of pollinators like bees differ from ours as humans, we can still strive to understand and appreciate them as individuals of other species – without anthropomorphizing them, Rönkä explains.

title: Ukrainan sota - yliopiston suositukset
content:
The University of Helsinki has condemned the military action by Russia and expressed its support for Ukraine and its university community. We have also expressed our support for Ukraine, together with other Finnish universities, through statements by and the . As a demonstration of support, we have illuminated buildings in the colours of the Ukrainian flag and raised the flag on our premises.

One of the principles of the University of Helsinki is to promote international collaboration in research and higher education, and to support these efforts even in difficult circumstances. Russia’s indefensible military aggression in Ukraine has required exceptional measures, which include those taken in the collaboration between universities.

The University of Helsinki is monitoring both national and EU-level sanctions, adapting our policies and processes accordingly. Together with other Finnish and international universities, the University of Helsinki strives to promote the end of military action in Ukraine, while supporting Ukrainian institutions and people.

title: REMM Project coordinated intensive courses in Mozambique and Madagascar
content:
TreesForDev project personnel, Marketta Vuola and Ossi Ollinaho also work with the REMM project. Many of the themes of the REMM project overlap with the TreesForDev project. 

Mozambique

The first training was organized at the Eduardo Mondlane University’s (UEM) Faculty of Agronomy and Forestry Engineering (FAEF) between August 31 and September 5, 2026. The training focused on forest restoration in miombo forest and mangroves and it gathered together professors, graduate students, researchers, and technicians from non-governmental organizations, as well as representatives of public and private institutions. The course aimed to strengthen the scientific, methodological, and practical skills of the participants for understanding the processes of ecosystem degradation and restoration, contributing to the training of specialists capable of responding to the challenges associated with climate change and biodiversity loss.

title: Tekoälyn käyttö herättää opettajissa uteliaisuutta ja huolta, ohjeistus käyttöönottoon puuttuu
content:
Generative AI in the form of applications that produce text and other content, also known as chatbots, have taken school life by storm. Public debate fluctuates between new opportunities and excitement, and concerns related to, among other things, environmental impact. 

This is evident in schools as well. According to a study conducted at the University of Helsinki, teachers’ emotions related to ChatGPT vary widely. Teachers find the use of AI applications equally fascinating and worrying.

According to the survey study conducted in three stages in 2023 and 2024, the positive emotions teachers experienced included in particular curiosity, excitement, interest and contemplation. Suspicion, worry, fear and frustration were the negative emotions highlighted most frequently.

Positive and negative emotions were reported nearly equally.

User experience was the single most important factor explaining differences in teachers’ emotions. The more personal experience teachers had with using ChatGPT or other AI applications, the more positively they viewed AI.

title: Maisteriohjelman opinnot käynnistyivät orientaatioviikolla Viikin kampuksella
content:
The first students of the Master's Programme in Technologies for Sustainable Use of Renewable Resources arrived in Viikki on Monday and were greeted by student tutors. On Tuesday, the Faculty of Agriculture and Forestry held its welcome event for all incoming master's students.

Students had the chance to get to know one another and familiarise themselves with the campus and induction activities.

Wednesday’s programme day began with morning coffee at the EE-building, where staff presented the programme’s specialisation modules, the structure of the studies and features such as field periods and cooperation with companies. The day also included work on course selections and an introduction to the Sisu system. In the afternoon, attendees networked with faculty and programme staff at the Forest Sciences Building; snacks and Finnish treats were provided.

Towards the end of the orientation week there was a Check‑in event for international students at the City Centre Campus, offering an introduction to various student organisations, Finnish student life and practical matters for those arriving in Finland.

title: Learnings from the Urban Mushroom Upcycling Operations pilot
content:
At first, a brewery and a mushroom farm might not seem to have much in common. One produces beer. The other grows fungi.

But in Viikki, University of Helsinki students tested what happens when the two are connected and when the mycelia – i.e. the mushroom spawn – becomes part of an even bigger loop.

From May to September 2026, a group of University of Helsinki students calling themselves the Shroomhead crew (Milla Tammivuori, Volter Kaitila, Silver De Vries, Sanni Taba and Amanda Tikkanen) took part in the Urban Mushroom Upcycling Operations Pilot, an experiment in local food production, circular bioeconomy and urban upcycling.

Coordinated by the Viikki Food Design Factory, this pilot brought together students, university researchers and local companies, Helsieni and CoolHead Brew. Together, they explored whether mushroom cultivation, food production and material experimentation could be interconnected into a local, urban circular operation.

The idea is simple. Grow mushrooms locally. Eat them locally. Then ask what can be done with what is left.

title: Call for talks and posters: HELDIG Summit 2026 Methodological encounters
content:
We are gathering speakers and poster proposals for the next HELDIG Summit that aims to provide a snapshot of digital research in SSH today. To bring about discussion, we are planning three themes: digital history, digital social sciences and digital heritage. We invite you to contribute to this event with a 5 minute flash-talk or poster from recent or ongoing project(s). The Summit is a good opportunity to give visibility to your latest research and tools, get inspired by methodological innovations in similar fields, and make new connections. 

The HELDIG Summit brings together social sciences and humanities in a day that takes a snapshot at the state of the art in digital research. This year, we bring discussion around methodological and infrastructure encounters beyond disciplines. What challenges in data processing new methods enable us to overcome? How to maintain and adapt our research tools to fast-changing technological landscape? How to target the use of AI responsibly in the research cycle? 

The Summit will take place on December 4 (we aim for a full-day 10:00-18:00), after which there will be a cocktail reception.
